answer: The data objects are tagged `#meta/library/remote`, and each needs a `name` and a `uri` attribute. The repository page itself is tagged `#meta/repository`.

## Which tag marks the data objects inside a repository page that point at installable libraries?

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Library/Development.md] ---
### Create a repository

# Create a repository
If you develop a few libraries, it may be good to make them more discoverable. To do so, you can group them in a [[Repository|Repository]].

For this, create another page in your space, this time under `Repository/`, e.g. `Repository/myuser` and tag it with `#meta/repository`.

In the page body, put a list of all your libraries, encoded as [[Tag/data|data objects]] as follows:

    ---
    tags: meta/repository
    ---
    This is my curated list of awesome libraries!

    ```#meta/library/remote
    name: Library1
    description: This is my first awesome library
    website: http://url.com/to/docs
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library1.md
    ---
    name: Library2
    description: This is my second awesome library
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library2.md
    ```

Required keys are:
* `name`: a descriptive name of your library.
  **Note**: this name is _not_ used as an installation location, the installation location is determined by the `name` key in the library itself.
* `uri`: The URI to install the library from.

Additional recommended keys are:
* `description`: a more elaborate description of the library and its functionality
* `author`: who developed this library
* `website`: a website URL for more information

Now share this repo page using [[Share]] to the same github repo (or any other, it doesn’t really matter), and call it `REPO.md` (by convention).

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Repository.md] ---
### Untitled

Repositories are a collection of _pointers_ to [[Library|Libraries]] to install. Their purpose is to offer a curated list of libraries to install.

By default, SilverBullet ships with two repositories: [[^Repositories/Std]] with a curated selection of community libraries, and [[^Repositories/SilverBulletMD]] with optional libraries maintained by the SilverBullet project. More can be installed via the [[Workbench/Libraries|Library Manager]].

The built-in repositories update like any other: the first update stores a copy in your space, which from then on takes the place of the shipped version. Deleting that copy brings the shipped version back, so built-in repositories can’t be removed.

Repositories are implemented on top of a few SilverBullet mechanisms, specifically they are simply [[Meta Page|Meta Pages]] tagged with `#meta/repository` that contain [[Tag/data|data objects]] tagged with `#meta/library/remote` with a `name` and `uri` attribute. Libraries are kept up to date using the [[Share]] mechanism.

### Scope rules

# Scope rules
* If a hashtag is the only content in a paragraph (at most with additional hashtags), it applies to the **page**.
* If a hashtag is used inside of an item (bullet point, or ordered list), it applies to that **item**.
* If a hashtag is used inside of a [[Task]], it applies to that **task**.
* If a hashtag is used inside of a paragraph, they apply to the **paragraph**.
* If a hashtag is used inside of a heading, it applies to that **header**.
* If a hashtag is used inside of a table row, it applies to that **table** row.
* If you create a [[Markdown/Fenced Code Block]] with a hashtag as language, it doesn’t attach a user tag: the hashtag becomes the [[Tag#Root tags|root tag]] of the [[Tag/data|data objects]] in the block.

--- [vault:corpus/docs/Workbench/Libraries.md] ---
### Untitled

The Libraries tab manages the [[Library|libraries]] in your space. In a read-only space it only shows what’s there: installing, updating, removing and checking for updates are hidden, with a note saying why (a read-only server doesn’t reach other servers, so there is nothing to check against). It reloads every time you show the tab, so what you see matches your space.

${widgets.commandButton("Workbench: Libraries")} opens this tab in the [[Workbench]].

The toolbar has:

* **Filter libraries**: narrows installed libraries by name and available ones by name, description and page.
* **Install…**: asks for a library or plug URI (`https://…` or `github:…`) and installs it. For a plug (a URI ending in `.plug.js`) it also asks where to save it.
* **Add repository…**: asks for a [[Repository]] URI and the page to put it on, then adds it so its libraries show up under Available.
* **Check for updates**: compares each installed library and repository with its source, and shows the result beside it (see below).
* **Update all**: updates every installed library that can be updated, with progress. It only shows when there is something to update.

Below it are three sections, each with its own error and info banner:

* **Installed**: the libraries you installed, plus plugs that no library brought along. Built-in libraries (on `Library/Std/` pages, or without a share URI) are marked *built-in* and can’t be updated or removed. Libraries in dev mode are marked *dev mode* and are left alone,

### Spaces

# Spaces
Spaces have a name and point to a folder where its content is kept. By default this will be inside the SilverBullet data folder, but you can pick any folder you like.
